steps.title: Store the proxy key
steps.text: In its own file, readable only by root. Keep it out of version control.
steps.label: Terminal
steps.code:
sudo install -m 600 -o root -g root /dev/null /etc/nginx/fingerly-proxy-key.conf
echo 'set $fingerly_proxy_key "fly_px_production_…";' | sudo tee /etc/nginx/fingerly-proxy-key.conf >/dev/null

steps.text: Run sudo systemctl edit caddy and add these lines. The key belongs in the environment of the Caddy process, never in the Caddyfile.

Environment=FINGERLY_PROXY_KEY=fly_px_production_…

steps.label: Terminal

steps.text: CloudFront > Functions > Create function, runtime cloudfront-js-2.0. Paste this, save and publish.
steps.label: function.js

steps.title: Add the origin
steps.text: In the distribution that serves your site. CloudFront always overwrites a viewer-sent header of the same name.
steps.label: Origin
steps.code:
Origin domain:  api.fingerly.io
Protocol:       HTTPS only
Custom header:  x-fingerly-proxy-key = fly_px_production_…

steps.title: Add the cache behavior
steps.text: Associate the function with both the viewer request and the viewer response.
steps.label: Cache behavior
steps.code:
Path pattern:            /k7x2qm4a
Origin:                  api.fingerly.io
Viewer protocol policy:  HTTPS only
Allowed HTTP methods:    GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PUT, POST, PATCH, DELETE
Cache policy:            CachingDisabled
Origin request policy:   AllViewerExceptHostHeader
Viewer request:          CloudFront Functions, the function above
Viewer response:         CloudFront Functions, the function above

steps.title: Save the service
steps.text: Save this as server.mjs in an empty folder.
steps.label: server.mjs

steps.title: Save its Dockerfile
steps.text: Beside server.mjs. The image has no dependencies and runs as an unprivileged user.
steps.label: Dockerfile
steps.code:
# Fingerly first-party proxy container, version 1.0.0.
# No dependencies to install: the image is Node and one file, run as the
# image's unprivileged `node` user. Numeric, so Kubernetes' runAsNonRoot can
# check it.
FROM node:24-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY server.mjs ./
ENV NODE_ENV=production PORT=8080
USER 1000:1000
EXPOSE 8080
CMD ["node", "server.mjs"]

steps.title: Build and run it
steps.text: Take the key from your secret store. remote trusts the connection address; behind a proxy use header:<name> for a header that proxy overwrites, or xff:<n> for the n-th X-Forwarded-For entry from the right.
steps.label: Terminal
steps.code:
docker build -t site-relay .
export FINGERLY_PROXY_KEY='fly_px_production_…'
docker run -d --name site-relay --restart unless-stopped -p 8080:8080 \
  -e FINGERLY_PATH=/k7x2qm4a -e FINGERLY_PROXY_KEY \
  -e FINGERLY_CLIENT_IP_SOURCE=remote \
  site-relay

steps.title: Route the path to it
steps.text: From the proxy or load balancer in front, send exactly this path on your site's host to the container, POST bodies included.
steps.label: Routing
steps.code: POST https://www.example.com/k7x2qm4a  ->  http://site-relay:8080/k7x2qm4a

# Fingerly first-party proxy container, version 1.0.0.
# No dependencies to install: the image is Node and one file, run as the
# image's unprivileged `node` user. Numeric, so Kubernetes' runAsNonRoot can
# check it.
FROM node:24-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY server.mjs ./
ENV NODE_ENV=production PORT=8080
USER 1000:1000

steps.title: Add it to your compose project
steps.text: In the project Traefik routes with its Docker provider, on a network Traefik can reach. Add entrypoints and tls labels if your other routers have them.
steps.label: docker-compose.yml
steps.code:
# Fingerly first-party proxy behind Traefik, version 1.0.0.
#
# Add this service to the compose project Traefik already routes with its
# Docker provider. `/k7x2qm4a` is the path the Fingerly dashboard issued; the
# router answers exactly that path and sends it to the container, which
# forwards the browser SDK's submissions to the Fingerly API. Put the
# container template's Dockerfile and server.mjs in ./site-relay.
services:
  site-relay:
    build: ./site-relay
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      FINGERLY_PATH: /k7x2qm4a
      # Traefik replaces X-Real-Ip with the address of the connection it
      # accepted. Read the README before trusting forwarded headers upstream.
      FINGERLY_CLIENT_IP_SOURCE: header:x-real-ip
      # From the shell or an .env file kept out of version control.
      FINGERLY_PROXY_KEY: ${FINGERLY_PROXY_KEY:?set FINGERLY_PROXY_KEY}
    labels:
      - "traefik.enable=true"
      - "traefik.http.routers.site-relay.rule=Path(`/k7x2qm4a`)"
      # Above your site's catch-all router, whatever its rule length.
      - "traefik.http.routers.site-relay.priority=10000"
      - "traefik.http.services.site-relay.loadbalancer.server.port=8080"

steps.title: Start it
steps.text: Take the key from your secret store or an .env file kept out of version control.
steps.label: Terminal
steps.code: FINGERLY_PROXY_KEY='fly_px_production_…' docker compose up -d --build site-relay

steps.title: Point the browser SDK at the path
steps.text: Pass the path as the endpoint. The SDK posts to it exactly as given.
steps.label: JavaScript

steps.title: Save the service
steps.text: Save this as server.mjs in an empty folder.
steps.label: server.mjs

steps.title: Save its package.json
steps.text: Beside server.mjs. Buildpacks build the service from it; no Dockerfile is needed.
steps.label: package.json

steps.title: Store the proxy key
steps.text: In Secret Manager, readable by the service's runtime service account.
steps.label: Terminal
steps.code:
printf '%s' 'fly_px_production_…' | gcloud secrets create first-party-relay-key --data-file=-
gcloud secrets add-iam-policy-binding first-party-relay-key \
  --member=serviceAccount:PROJECT_NUMBER-compute@developer.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor

steps.title: Deploy
steps.text: From the folder. The ingress setting means only your load balancer can reach it.
steps.label: Terminal
steps.code:
gcloud run deploy site-relay --source . --region=europe-west1 \
  --ingress=internal-and-cloud-load-balancing --allow-unauthenticated \
  --set-env-vars=FINGERLY_PATH=/k7x2qm4a \
  --set-secrets=FINGERLY_PROXY_KEY=first-party-relay-key:latest

steps.title: Add it to your load balancer
steps.text: A serverless NEG and a backend service. Use the scheme your load balancer uses: EXTERNAL_MANAGED, or EXTERNAL for the classic one.
steps.label: Terminal
steps.code:
gcloud compute network-endpoint-groups create site-relay-neg \
  --region=europe-west1 --network-endpoint-type=serverless \
  --cloud-run-service=site-relay
gcloud compute backend-services create site-relay-backend \
  --global --load-balancing-scheme=EXTERNAL_MANAGED
gcloud compute backend-services add-backend site-relay-backend \
  --global --network-endpoint-group=site-relay-neg \
  --network-endpoint-group-region=europe-west1

steps.title: Route the path to it
steps.text: In the URL map that serves your site. If your host already has a path matcher, add a path rule for /k7x2qm4a to it instead (Load balancing > Edit > Routing rules).
steps.label: Terminal
steps.code:
gcloud compute url-maps add-path-matcher URL_MAP --global \
  --path-matcher-name=site --default-service=YOUR_SITE_BACKEND \
  --new-hosts=www.example.com --path-rules=/k7x2qm4a=site-relay-backend
